Subject: POC intake: workload profile & success criteria — Fresno Health

Hi Samira / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment before we draft the POC plan. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of goals
- Success criteria (proposed):
  1) 95th percentile latency under 300ms for interactive triage flows (50–150 tokens output).
  2) Token cost <= $0.002/token equivalent for inference during steady-state.
  3) No user-visible errors for >99.9% of production-like traffic during the 2-week ramp.
- Key evaluation: functional fidelity on clinical summarization tests + latency/cost targets.

Workload intake we need from you (if you can paste answers into your reply that helps):
- Peak RPS and typical RPS (per endpoint)
- Average/conversational token lengths for prompts and responses (mean and 95th pct)
- Expected concurrent users/sessions and per-session request cadence
- Burst pattern examples (duration, multiplier over baseline) — e.g., morning triage spike: 2x for 12m.
- A sample endpoint or two and whether you’ll route sensitive PHI for the POC

Proposed ownership & timeline
- Redwood lead: me (aditya) — commercial + timeline owner
- Technical lead: Monica (CS/engops) — infra, sizing, onboarding
- Success: joint sign-off on acceptance evaluation after 2-week ramp (engineering + product)
- Target kickoff: week of Mar 1; 4-week POC (1w infra + onboarding, 2w ramp, 1w acceptance)

I attached a simple intake spreadsheet (fresno-workload-intake.xlsx) you can fill if easier.

Next steps: can you (1) confirm the proposed success criteria and (2) paste the workload answers above? Once we have those Monica will scope the infra and propose instance counts / pre-warming.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira@fresnohealth.com>

Date: Sun, 21 Feb 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC intake: workload profile & success criteria — Fresno Health

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear summary. Confirming the success criteria looks good to us with one tweak: can we move the latency target to 350ms p95 for the first 2 weeks while ramping (we can tighten on acceptance).

Answers below (high-level — attached a short sample log export as well):
- Typical RPS (all endpoints combined): 12 RPS steady, peaks to ~48 RPS during morning triage windows (06:30–07:15 local).
- Per-endpoint: /summarize (majority) ~8 RPS steady, /assist ~3 RPS, /batch-reporting ~1 RPS.
- Token lengths:
  - Prompts: mean 60 tokens, 95th 220 tokens
  - Responses: mean 90 tokens, 95th 320 tokens
- Concurrency: expected 30 concurrent sessions during steady-state, up to 120 during peaks (bursts last ~10–20 minutes).
- Burst patterns: morning spike 4x baseline for ~45 minutes; occasional midday blips 2–3x for ~10 minutes (we'll provide traces).
- PHI: POC traffic will include de-identified PHI; full PHI is out of scope for the demo environment.

Attached: api_traffic_snapshot.csv (anonymized sample). Let us know if you want raw logs or a subset of request/response pairs.

On timing — Mar 1 kickoff works for us, and we can commit two engineering SMEs for the first week for onboarding.

—Samira
Director of Clinical Informatics
Fresno Health

Thanks Samira — this is really helpful. A couple clarifying questions and a proposed operational plan below.

Clarifications
- When you say "de-identified PHI" — can you confirm no free-text identifiers remain in the POC payloads? That affects our logging/retention defaults.
- For /batch-reporting endpoint: are requests typically bulk requests with larger token outputs (e.g., >1k tokens)? That will change memory/KV cache sizing.

Proposed POC ops plan (high-level)
- Week 0 (pre-kick): config review + data handling agreement (security/compliance skim) — Monica lead
- Week 1 (kickoff + onboarding): instance provisioning + sample replay — Monica + Fresno SMEs
- Week 2–3 (ramp): simulate production bursts and run evaluation prompts; collect latency/cost metrics
- Week 4 (acceptance): run the acceptance test set (clinical summarization suite) and sign off

Sizing notes (initial guess from Samira's numbers)
- Baseline: 12 RPS, mean output 90 tokens -> estimate 2 dedicated g4dn-like instances for steady-state with autoscale to handle 48 RPS peaks; final sizing will depend on model selection and quantization profile.
- For batch-reporting: if outputs >1k tokens, we recommend separate batch nodes to avoid blocking interactive capacity.

Action items
- Monica: draft infra runbook and instance count + pre-warm plan by Tue Feb 23
- Samira/Tom: confirm de-identification level and whether you can share a 1-hour window of raw (anonymized) traces
- Aditya: I'll work with you to lock the kickoff calendar invite after Monica posts the runbook

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
